Choosing the best app depends on what you value most, but when evaluating them strictly as a **main UK current account** (where your salary lands and bills are paid), **Starling Bank is the overall winner.** 

---

### 1. Starling Bank — Best Overall Main Account
* **The Verdict:** The closest thing to a traditional high-street bank, but with the convenience and speed of a modern app.
* **Why it wins as a main account:**
  * **Core Banking Basics:** It supports the **Current Account Switch Service (CASS)**, making it painless to move your existing balance and Direct Debits over.
  * **Cash & Cheques:** You can deposit cash at any Post Office (free up to £1,000 per calendar year) and pay in cheques by snapping a photo in the app.
  * **Safety & Reliability:** Fully licensed UK bank with full FSCS protection. It consistently ranks at or near the very top of official CMA customer satisfaction surveys and offers 24/7 UK-based customer support.
  * **Overdrafts & Web Access:** Offers arranged overdrafts and a secure web-browser portal if you lose your phone.
* **Drawbacks:**
  * No regular card cashback rewards.
  * Its savings interest rates are decent, but rarely market-leading compared to dedicated easy-access savings accounts.

---

### 2. Chase UK — Best for Daily Spending & Rewards
* **The Verdict:** Phenomenal perks and savings, but missing a couple of essential everyday banking features needed to be your *only* account.
* **Strengths:**
  * **Perks:** 1% cashback on eligible debit card spending (up to £15/month).
  * **Savings:** Excellent linked easy-access savings rates and a popular 5% AER round-up account.
  * **Safety:** Fully licensed UK bank under JPMorgan Chase with FSCS protection.
  * **Switching:** Supports CASS if you want to switch automated payments in.
* **Drawbacks as a main account:**
  * **No Cash or Cheques:** Chase does **not** accept cash deposits or cheque deposits. If a relative sends a cheque or you are given cash, you have no way to deposit it.
  * **No Overdrafts:** There is no safety buffer if an unexpected Direct Debit comes through.
  * App-only (no desktop banking) and slightly stricter automated fraud blocks on certain transfers.

---

### 3. Revolut — Best for Travel & Multi-Currency (Not Main UK Banking)
* **The Verdict:** An incredible multi-currency and travel tool, but still awkward as a sole UK primary current account.
* **Strengths:**
  * **FX & Travel:** The ability to hold, exchange, and spend in dozens of currencies at competitive interbank rates.
  * **Features:** Disposable virtual cards, budgeting tools, split bills, and investment features in one app.
* **Drawbacks as a main account:**
  * **No CASS:** Revolut does not participate in the Current Account Switch Service, so you have to move your salary, bills, and standing orders manually.
  * **Feature Gating:** The best perks (insurance, high ATM limits, lounge passes) require costly monthly subscription tiers (Plus, Premium, Metal, Ultra).
  * **Limitations:** The free tier adds markups to foreign exchange on weekends and limits monthly free currency conversions. Customer support is primarily chatbot-driven and can be difficult to navigate if your account is flagged.

---

### Summary Comparison

| Feature | Starling | Chase | Revolut |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FSCS Protection** | Yes | Yes | Yes (rolling out via bank licence) |
| **Current Account Switch (CASS)** | Yes | Yes | No |
| **Cash Deposits** | Yes (Post Office) | No | Limited / Third-party |
| **Cheque Imaging** | Yes | No | No |
| **Debit Card Cashback** | No | 1% (capped at £15/mo) | No (except specific merchant offers) |
| **Arranged Overdraft** | Yes | No | No standard UK overdraft |
| **Web Browser Access** | Yes | No | Limited |
